RULED by the design lane (1.0.0_SA_CTO~X, 2026-08-28 15:1xZ) on the WP-3b finding 0.4.0_DT_ClientPlatform~X 78074 (uniform gap: entity_class / plane / entity_grain / identity_scope / identity_policy missing on 42 of 42 parts -- two schemas never joined). This file is the translator's DECLARED INPUT: every value it yields carries basis 'held' with this file's path @commit as the evidence, never 'measured'. It is NOT a bundle member (bundle_identity.py's member list governs); the contract (v0.3-candidate+27) does not move. sources.planes: org/tier2_senior/0.4.0_DT_ClientPlatform/deliverables/D11_L1/L1_CANONICAL_GRAIN_DECLARATION.md @16cd74c870 -- FOUR canonical grains, one per plane: symbol, file, arn_resource, chain_motif
sources.manifest_vocabulary: org/standards/L0_GRAPH_SUBSTRATE_MANIFEST.schema.json #/$defs/part (part_class enum: store | materializer | projection | reader_tool | spec_artifact | output_artifact | other; home_space enum: repo_path | s3_uri | iceberg_table | none)

entity_class.why: A manifest part is an L0 REGISTRY object -- the entity class the ISCK registry already carries for exactly this ('part'). The manifest's part_class (store / materializer / projection / ...) is a GRAPH-OBJECT taxonomy, not the identity taxonomy: mapping it onto entity_class because both end in 'class' is the substitution DT~X refused (78074) and this ruling refuses. The part_class travels on the entity_binding's native key context and on the manifest itself; a finer entity class for a part (e.g. 'store' for a store part) is a LATER declaration act with its own evidence, never this mapping's default.

entity_grain.why: The L0 registry's own grain. L1's per-plane grains (symbol / file / arn_resource / chain_motif) apply to the parts' MEMBERS (member_set), which this slice does not admit. A part admitted at grain 'part' makes no claim about its members' identities.

identity_scope.why: A registry part is a logical object; its fabric/device/run instances are surface_versions and materialization_runs, which carry their own scopes. Closed enum satisfied.

plane.why: A part's plane is the plane of its HOME: a repo path lives in L1's file plane; an S3 object and an Iceberg/Nessie table are cloud resources (L1: 'arn_resource -- a cloud resource'). A part with NO home fits none of L1's four planes and is NOT forced into one: it is carried under the declared token 'unplaced' (a NEW token, census 0 at ruling time) and, by the identity_policy rule below, admitted as held_for_adjudication -- comparable within no plane until a later declaration places it. That is the L1 declaration's own posture: cross-plane comparison only through a declared bridge, never a parse or a guess.

identity_policy.why: The identity of a repo-homed part follows the repository's history; the identity of a cloud-homed part follows the provider's key (bucket/key; table identifier); a part with no home has no key space to follow and is held for adjudication -- the registry's own value for exactly this. All four values are registered identity policies; none is minted here.

basis_and_evidence.evidence: this file's path @ the commit that lands it, plus the ruling record; the translator prints, per admitted part, the five values and this file's digest; a part admitted under held_for_adjudication prints as such and counts in the ADMITTED denominator with its policy named -- never silently as 'resolved'
basis_and_evidence.status_basis_on_the_entity: authored (the values are declared, not derived by a fold)

denominators_at_ruling: printed in the ruling record from the pinned manifest (parts by part_class x home_space); the translator re-derives them at run time and prints its own line -- a typed count on this file is not the number
contestable: every value here is a claim a later contest_event can target (the contract's own mechanism); a KILL of a row is a finding against this file routed to the design lane, and moves mapping_version
